narrative:
The 2020 St. Louis Cardinals played one of the most unusual seasons in modern baseball history, navigating a COVID-19 outbreak that wiped out nearly two weeks of their schedule and forced them into a frantic sprint just to qualify for the expanded postseason. Starting 2-3 in July, they entered August already behind the eight ball, and the early days of that month were haunted by bullpen meltdowns — Tyler Webb surrendering a three-run shot to David Bote and then a grand slam to Matt Davidson in the span of four days — that threatened to sink the season before it truly began.

Yet the Cardinals steadied themselves through August and September, going a combined 28-25 across those two months to claw their way into playoff position. The offense was thin — a .694 OPS tells the story — but flashes of brilliance carried them: Tyler O'Neill delivered clutch hits, Harrison Bader sparked rallies with his legs, and veterans like Yadier Molina and Brad Miller came through in critical moments. The pitching staff, anchored by a rotation that kept runs manageable with a 3.90 ERA, gave the team a chance night after night even as the bullpen remained a source of anxiety throughout September.

The final weeks of September saw the Cardinals gut out a 17-15 record, good enough to earn a Wild Card berth, though the journey was littered with late-inning heartbreak. Giovanny Gallegos and Ryan Helsley both had costly outings, and the offense too often went quiet when it mattered most. Still, Yadier Molina's two-run homer on September 20th was a reminder that this club had a pulse, and Paul Goldschmidt's blast in the Wild Card opener briefly stirred hope of a deep run.

But the postseason was swift and brutal. The San Diego Padres — fueled by a young Fernando Tatis Jr., who homered twice in Game 2 — proved too powerful for a Cardinals roster running on fumes. Daniel Ponce de Leon and Giovanny Gallegos were hammered by the Padres' potent lineup in the elimination games, and St. Louis was bounced in the Wild Card round without advancing. It was a bittersweet end to a season that deserved credit simply for being completed, but the Cardinals left San Diego knowing they needed more firepower — and a more reliable bullpen — to compete in October.

chapters.title: Stumbling Out of the Gate
chapters.description: Early bullpen disasters and a COVID-disrupted schedule leave the Cardinals scrambling just to stay afloat.

chapters.title: Finding Footing
chapters.description: The Cardinals stabilize behind timely hitting from O'Neill and Bader, scratching their way back toward respectability.

chapters.title: Grinding Through September
chapters.description: A winning September record masks persistent late-inning troubles as St. Louis fights to secure a playoff spot.

chapters.title: A Glimmer of Hope
chapters.description: Molina's home run and Helsley's clutch save briefly lift the Cardinals as they punch their postseason ticket.

chapters.title: October Ends Quickly
chapters.description: The Wild Card round against San Diego opens with promise but Tatis and the Padres offense overwhelm a depleted Cardinals pitching staff.
